perspective:
Christian’s available information:

- He is Christian Mensah, a Black male police officer with a high school education. He has been childhood friends with Jonathan Balogun; he often seeks Jonathan’s advice and values his perspective.
- He recently felt Jonathan was hiding something important, which made him anxious and suspicious. He arranged a meeting with Jonathan at their favorite coffee shop to confront him.
- Christian told Jonathan he felt Jonathan was hiding something. He heard Jonathan say he could trust him, then Jonathan admitted he had been keeping something: he is in trouble and did not know how to tell Christian.
- Christian felt worried and empathetic. He offered help and support. He heard Jonathan say the situation is complicated, that he does not want to drag Christian into it, and that he could use support and resources to get out of the mess.
- Christian came to believe Jonathan’s trouble might involve criminal activity. He asked Jonathan if it was illegal. He heard Jonathan say he could not be sure, that he might have gotten involved with the wrong people, but that he did not do anything illegal himself. Christian decided to investigate discreetly; Jonathan thanked him and said he trusted him to handle it carefully.
- Christian’s investigation led him to believe/state that Jonathan is being framed. He told Jonathan someone is trying to set him up. He said he had leads and planned to gather more evidence to prove Jonathan’s innocence.
- Christian now believes he has found out who is behind it: someone close to both him and Jonathan, someone they both know and trust. He feels betrayed and resolute. He told Jonathan he would confront this person and bring them to justice. Jonathan warned him the person is dangerous and trusted Christian to do the right thing.
- The specific identity/name of the culprit is not given in the available text, so Christian’s available information includes only his belief that he has identified someone close to them.
